title: Migrating Older PHP Code
keywords: legacy php, migration, and professional development
learning_outcomes: Explain what migrating older php code contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: incremental migration.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Legacy maintenance preserves real behavior while removing risky assumptions. Use tests to make changes incremental, check the supported PHP/dependency matrix, and migrate deprecated patterns with a documented plan. In this lesson, focus on incremental migration; then compare it with compatibility testing. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use migrating older php code when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Legacy maintenance preserves real behavior while removing risky assumptions. Use tests to make changes incremental, check the supported PHP/dependency matrix, and migrate deprecated patterns with a documented plan. For migrating older php code, begin with incremental migration. Also distinguish compatibility testing; replacing deprecated apis; updating dependencies. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: Incremental migration
items.text: Know when to use incremental migration, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

items.title: Compatibility testing
items.text: Write an assertion about observable behavior and include a boundary or failure case; a passing command alone does not prove the requirement.

items.title: Replacing deprecated APIs
items.text: Expect network failures and malformed responses; validate the response, set bounded timeouts, and make repeat delivery safe where needed.

items.title: Updating dependencies
items.text: Know when to use updating dependencies, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

items.title: Preserving existing application behavior
items.text: Know when to use preserving existing application behavior, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Migrating Older PHP Code
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$json = "{\"items\":[1,2,3]}";
$payload = json_decode($json, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
echo count($payload["items"]) . " items" . PHP_EOL;

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Change legacy code incrementally, use tests to preserve behavior, and verify the target PHP/dependency compatibility matrix.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for migrating older php code from top to bottom. Start by identifying incremental migration, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.

summary: Migrating Older PHP Code is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
Prefer explicit behavior and testable examples over implicit assumptions.
Change legacy code incrementally, use tests to preserve behavior, and verify the target PHP/dependency compatibility matrix.
